title: Utilization velocity tranche pricing playbook
summary: Draft spreadsheet & playbook for pricing reserved GPU capacity via time-limited tranches tied to utilization velocity, plus backfill credits and resale hedging. Includes tab layout, example calculations, experiment matrix and recommended guardrails.
body:
Purpose and overview:
This is a working sheet + playbook to experiment with tranche-based reserved capacity pricing where price and credit allocation are a function of utilization velocity (rate of change of pool utilization) rather than only static committed capacity. Goal: reduce idle waste, surface short-term supply opportunities, and align customer incentives to smooth spikes while preserving predictable revenue for Redwood Dedicated.

High-level idea (one sentence):
Offer time-limited tranches (e.g., 30d, 90d, 180d) that provide a lower per-token/GPU-hour effective price when customers accept dynamic backfill and limited resale/transferability; tranche discount magnitude adjusts automatically based on recent utilization velocity signals.

Why this is different from existing commit models:
- Commit models tie price to volume and duration; tranche model ties incremental discounts to how quickly the pool is being utilized.
- When utilization is rising fast, tranche discounts shrink (protecting revenue). When utilization stalls or falls, deeper tranche discounts encourage new sticky buys and provide backfill liquidity.

Spreadsheet tabs (suggested):
1) assumptions - key inputs
2) utilization-signals - raw and smoothed utilization, velocity, acceleration
3) tranche-pricing - price schedule by tranche length and velocity bucket
4) backfill-credit - ledger for credits earned/consumed when backfill used
5) cohort-sim - simulated customer cohorts and cashflow over 12 months
6) experiments - A/B test matrix, metrics, and success criteria

Tab: assumptions (sample rows)
- baseline-gpu-hour-cost: 2.40
- fixed-overhead-per-call: 0.01
- target-utilization: 0.78
- smoothing-window-days: 7
- velocity-thresholds: "-0.03, 0.00, 0.03"

Tab: utilization-signals (example CSV snippet)
date,pool-utilization,util-7d-smoothed,util-velocity(7d)
2024-10-01,0.62,0.605,-0.004
2024-10-08,0.66,0.635,0.030
2024-10-15,0.71,0.687,0.052

Formula notes: util-velocity(7d) = (smoothed_today - smoothed_7d_ago) / smoothed_7d_ago. Use rolling EWMA alternative: =EXPONENTIAL_MOVING_AVERAGE(range,alpha).

Tab: tranche-pricing (concept)
Tranches: 30d, 90d, 180d. For each tranche length, define base discount and velocity-adjustment factor.
Columns: tranche_id, length_days, base_discount_pct, velocity_sensitivity, min_price_multiplier, max_price_multiplier
Example rows: 30,30,0.12, -0.4, 0.6, 1.05; 90,90,0.18,-0.6,0.5,1.03; 180,180,0.22,-0.8,0.45,1.02

Price calculation (plaintext formula):
observed_velocity = lookup_latest(util-velocity,window=7d)
adjustment = velocity_sensitivity * observed_velocity
price_multiplier = clamp(1 - base_discount_pct - adjustment, min_price_multiplier, max_price_multiplier)
effective_gpu_hour_price = baseline-gpu-hour-cost * price_multiplier

Backfill credit mechanics:
- When Redwood routes spare capacity to other tenants to honor a tranche buyer during a low-util period, the tranche buyer receives a small backfill credit (fraction of their commitment) to compensate for potential performance variance and to encourage acceptance of dynamic co-tenancy.
- Ledger columns: tranche_id, date, credit_amount_usd, reason, consumed_by_customer(Boolean).
- Credit expiry: default 90 days. Policy: credits cannot exceed 25% of tranche fee paid.

Cohort sim (short description):
- Inputs: cohort size, average GPU-hours/month, propensity-to-cancel as a function of observed latency/bursting events, probability-of-transfer/resale.
- Outputs: ARR contribution, expected utilization impact, churn delta vs static commit.
- Monte Carlo: simulate 1,000 draws of daily utilization and recompute tranche pricing weekly to capture feedback loops.

Experiment matrix (example rows):
- Hypothesis A: 30d tranche with velocity sensitivity -0.4 will increase pool utilization by 6–10% in low-demand months compared to baseline. Metric: change in weekly avg utilization + tranche churn rate.
- Hypothesis B: Backfill credits <=10% of tranche fee will not materially increase customer support tickets or perceived SLA erosion. Metric: ticket volume and NPS change.

Customer-facing terms (draft language):
- "Tranche reservations provide a discounted effective rate in exchange for limited dynamic placement: during low utilization windows, Redwood may place your workload alongside other compatible customers. You keep reserved access to capacity up to your tranche quota; occasional transient reroutes may occur to maintain latency SLOs. Backfill credits compensate for rare reroutes."

Risks & mitigations:
- Revenue leakage: cap maximum credit exposure and floor prices with min_price_multiplier.
- Customer confusion: default UI visuals showing "current tranche discount" and "current velocity signal"; require explicit opt-in for first 30d tranche purchase.
- Operational complexity: pilot with a single region and two GPU types (p6/rtx-style and a100-type) before broad rollout.

Next steps / action items:
- PM (Avery): build spreadsheet skeleton with tabs and formulas; deadline 2024-11-20.
- Finance (Diego): validate baseline-gpu-hour-cost and tax/overhead assumptions; deadline 2024-11-27.
- SRE (Priya): instrument utilization-signals and expose API for current velocity per pool; deadline 2024-12-04.
- Solutions Eng (Samira): draft customer FAQ and opt-in UI flows; deadline 2024-12-04.

Appendix: suggested visualizations in sheet UI
- Heatmap: utilization vs velocity buckets over last 6 months
- Line chart: effective_gpu_hour_price by tranche over time (overlay smoothed utilization)
- Waterfall: tranche revenue contributed vs credits consumed (monthly)

Notes-to-self / open questions (raw):
- Should tranche discounts be cumulative with other promotional credits? probably not by default.
- How to communicate velocity in console without exposing noisy real-time signals? show 7d-smoothed band with qualitative label (rising/flat/falling).
- Need legal review on resale/transferability language (transferable tranches might be a later product).

End of draft.
